text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Wolves host Everton at Molineux!
Wolves are looking to end 2023 with three successive wins after impressive victories over Chelsea and Brentford across the festive period lifted Gary O'Neil's men to 11th in the Premier League table.

Having seemingly left any fears of a relegation battle behind, Wolves are looking to extend their unbeaten run at Molineux to eight league games, with the likes of Manchester City, Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Tottenham and Chelsea all failing to win on the ground since the end of September.

Everton, by contrast, suffered back-to-back losses either side of Christmas, though there were positives for Sean Dyche to take from those games as the Toffees pushed Tottenham close before squandering a 1-0 lead in Wednesday's 3-1 loss to Manchester City.

With Luton Town suffering a spirited 3-2 defeat against Chelsea in Saturday's early game, Everton – who would be one point above their hosts if not for their 10-point deduction for breaching the Premier League's financial rules – have a chance to pull four points clear of the bottom three.
O'Neil makes two changes to the Wolves side which won 4-1 at Brentford on Wednesday.

Dawson returns after missing that game with a cut to his knee as Santiago Bueno drops to the bench, while Doyle comes into midfield with Mario Lemina absent following the death of his father this week.

Traore is back among the substitutes after being ill over the festive period, while Neto is still awaiting his first minutes since suffering a hamstring injury in October, having been an unused substitute last time out.
Everton's starting lineup also shows two changes to that which lost to City in midweek, with Beto and Andre Gomes dropping to the bench.
Calvert-Lewin and Keane are introduced, and it looks like Dyche will match O'Neil's 3-4-3 system for this one.
Abdoulaye Doucoure, Idrissa Gueye and Ashley Young are all absent for the Toffees.
Wolves are unbeaten in their last seven Premier League home games (four wins, three draws), last having a longer run without defeat at Molineux between January and August 2019 (10).
Will they maintain their fine form on their own turf? We're about to find out – kick-off is rapidly approaching!
We're under way at Molineux for the final time this year as Everton get the ball rolling, donning an all grey change kit for their last outing of 2023!
CHANCE! Hwang makes an excellent run in behind the Everton backline to pick up possession on the left side of the box.
He turns Keane inside-out before cutting back for Cunha, but Branthwaite makes a vital last-ditch clearance to stop the Brazilian from turning home! Bright start from the hosts!
Hwang stayed down in the aftermath of that early chance, but the South Korean is now up and moving freely.
It's a big boost for Wolves to have him fit for this game, after he was forced off with a back injury at Brentford.
He'll be leaving for the Asian Cup after this match.

Wolves have won four of their last five Premier League games against Everton (one draw), as many victories as they managed in their previous 21 league meetings with the Toffees (eight draws, nine losses).
A late header from Kalajdzic decided the reverse fixture at Goodison Park, with O'Neil claiming his first victory as Wolves boss by a 1-0 scoreline in August.
Applause breaks out at Molineux in the fifth minute as fans show their support for the team's number five Lemina.
He's not involved here following the death of his father yesterday, and the Wolves players are wearing black armbands to mark his loss.
WHAT A CHANCE FOR WOLVES! HOW IS IT NOT 1-0? McNeil sees a wide free-kick headed clear and Wolves break at devastating speed, with Cunha slipping Hwang through on goal.
He has the chance to shoot left-footed but instead sits Pickford down, only to take one touch too many and be crowded out by grey shirts.
That was a huge chance for Hwang, who was unusually hesitant to pull the trigger.
He already has 10 Premier League goals this season following his brace at Brentford last time out.
Patterson skips infield to play a neat give-and-go with Calvert-Lewin, but Wolves get numbers back and Tarkowski's eventual ball into the box is easily dealt with by Doyle.
It's been a rather scrappy opening to this game.
Sarabia, Semedo and Hwang are all involved as Wolves look to build down their right flank, but the latter gifts possession back to Everton with a slack pass.
Joao Gomes then recovers it for Wolves and is fouled by his opposite number Onana.
WIDE! Joao Gomes steals possession from Garner and Wolves quickly work it to Cunha.
He shoots early from all of 25 yards out, and it just dips wide of the bottom-right corner with Pickford scrambling across.
Wolves are showing some neat touches here without quite finding the final product in attack, while Everton still look to be getting to grips with this back-three system.
The Toffees attempt to break through Calvert-Lewin, but Dawson stops him in his tracks with a firm challenge.
Now Mykolenko is forced into action by Sarabia, sliding in with a well-timed challenge to stop the Spaniard in his tracks just inside Everton's area – he had to get that one right!
Everton threaten as McNeil skips through the Wolves midfield before looking to play in Calvert-Lewin, but he just gets too much on his throughball, allowing Sa to claim it.
There's a brief moment of concern for Everton with Tarkowski down on his haunches.
He looks to be holding his chest, but he's soon back up and looks okay to continue.
Wolves aren't happy as Semedo looks to break beyond Mykolenko, who appears to grab the wing-back's arm and send him to the turf.
The referee declines to award a free-kick, as Semedo may not have kept his heavy touch in play anyway.
Wolves have managed 10 touches in Everton's area so far, with the Toffees only recording one at the other end.
McNeil sets his sights from range, but he sends his powerful 25-yard effort comfortably over Sa's crossbar.
Patterson receives the first yellow card of the game, having impeded Joao Gomes to stop a flowing Wolves move.
Everton were in danger of being caught short there following some good play by Cunha, so their right wing-back took one for the team.
Semedo wins the first corner of the game on the Wolves right.
Sarabia swings it into the area... where Dawson flicks it off Tarkowski and behind for another set-piece.
GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLLLL! KILMAN PUTS WOLVES 1-0 AHEAD! Everton deal with the second Wolves corner, but not the subsequent ball back into the area from Cunha.

Pickford makes a fine reflex save to deny Dawson's attempt, clawing it off the line, but Kilman is there to prod home the rebound and open the scoring! The Wolves captain then holds Lemina's shirt aloft as the hosts celebrate – a classy gesture.
That was just Kilman's second Premier League goal, and both have come against Everton!
CHANCE! That's as close as Everton have come! McNeil finds a pocket of space, turning to play Calvert-Lewin in down the right-hand channel.
The angle is tight, and the striker has to flick it over Sa, but it just drifts across goal and away with no team-mate there to attack it.
Wolves have now scored in each of their last 17 Premier League home games – they last had a longer scoring streak at Molineux in the top flight between April 1965 and April 1968 (22 games).
CLOSE! Cunha drives upfield for Wolves again before offloading for Doyle.
He feeds his pass out to Semedo, who flashes the ball across the face of goal, and Sarabia is just unable to get a touch! Another good chance for the hosts.
Kilman is perhaps fortunate to win a free-kick near his own corner flag, having gone down easily under pressure from McNeil.
There's a slight concern for Everton as Onana goes down with nobody around him inside his own half.
He's quickly back to his feet, but he seems to be moving somewhat awkwardly.
This is the eighth consecutive calendar year in which Everton's final league game is away from home.
They're unbeaten in their last four, beating Newcastle United in 2019, Sheffield United in 2020 and drawing with Chelsea and Manchester City in 2021 and 2022 respectively.
Everton are enjoying a more sustained spell of possession now, with Wolves seemingly happy to sit off a little more after opening the scoring.
The Toffees are moving it well without really making any headway.
Semedo slips a neat pass down the line for Cunha, who drives a low cross into the area.
Tarkowski flicks out a heel and diverts it towards the edge of the box, where Sarabia is penalised for a foul on Keane.
Onana is down again, and this could spell the end of his involvement.
It seems he was caught on the heel by Semedo a few minutes ago, and Dyche now has Andre Gomes out warming up.
Onana goes off the pitch after receiving treatment, but the Belgian will re-enter the fray to give it another go.
Dyche will be desperate to avoid losing his influential midfielder.
Hwang darts down the left flank to latch onto Toti's clearance, getting there ahead of Tarkowski before being fouled from behind by the former Burnley man.
Wolves get a free-kick near the corner flag, with Sarabia stood over the dead ball.
Sarabia's deep cross is punched clear by Pickford, who takes out his own team-mate Branthwaite in the process.
Hwang is then penalised for a foul as Everton get a free-kick inside their own half.
Ait-Nouri is booked for delaying the restart as Everton attempt to take a right-wing throw-in.
He's the first Wolves player to see yellow.
Everton look to break down their right flank after Ait-Nouri cedes possession, but Calvert-Lewin overhits his pass for Harrison, and it runs out for a throw.
The visitors are yet to record a shot on target.
Good goalkeeping! Pickford has to remain alert to prevent Hwang reaching a long ball over the top, dashing off his line to make a crucial clearance near the edge of his own box.
Hwang has made plenty of theatening runs in behind the Everton backline so far.
We're into a minimum of four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this opening period.
Chance... but the flag is up! Onana plays a lovely ball in behind Dawson, sending Calvert-Lewin clean through.
However, the striker makes a meal of the chance, inviting Sa to smother the ball with an awkward touch, then the flag goes up against him anyway.
Everton win a corner on their left-hand side, which is delivered deep towards Branthwaite at the back post.
He causes something of a scramble with his header across goal, but Toti is eventually able to hammer a clearance upfield.
Wolves are closing in on half-time with a one-goal lead.
Calvert-Lewin catches Dawson with a trailing arm as the pair compete in the air.
The incident provokes something of a scuffle between Doyle and McNeil, and the Wolves man is booked.
McNeil is also booked for his role in that altercation.
HALF-TIME: WOLVES 1-0 EVERTON.
It's half-time at Molineux, and Kilman's goal is the difference after 45 minutes as Wolves lead Everton 1-0.

The hosts started brightly with Everton seemingly struggling to adjust after switching to a three-man backline, with Hwang failing to get a shot away when clean through early on before Cunha fired just wide from range.
The home side went ahead through their captain in the 25th minute, Kilman steering home the rebound after Pickford clawed Dawson's lunging effort off the line.
Wolves have failed to really threaten since then, but Everton are yet to manage a shot on target.
Dyche will demand more from his side after the restart, while O'Neil will be hoping for a repeat of an enterprising first 25 minutes from his men.
Stay tuned for the second half!
Cunha, Sarabia and Hwang have shown some bright flashes for Wolves, each attempting three dribbles – a joint-high tally among all players on the pitch.
The former pair have each played 10 passes in the final third, more than anyone else, and O'Neil will be hoping they can continue to drag Everton's defence around after the break.
Wolves also still have Neto in reserve, and he will be desperate to make an impact if called upon after two months on the sidelines.
Wolves get the ball rolling again for the second half, with no half-time changes made by either manager.

Wolves have avoided defeat in their last six Premier League matches when scoring the opening goal, though their last such loss did come when they last hosted a Merseyside club, going down 3-1 against Liverpool in September.
Almost! Dawson's sliced clearance is flicked wide by Sarabia, bringing Semedo into the game.
He mishits his cross from the right, but it almost dips over Pickford and into the far corner, just fading wide of the post!
Onana looks to have recovered from his earlier injury scare.
He plays a pass wide to Patterson, whose cross is sliced up in the air by Toti, forcing Sa into an unconvincing punch.
Joao Gomes follows up to complete the clearance.
Danger! A deep Everton free-kick causes carnage in the Wolves area, with Doyle and Dawson both going to ground to block close-range efforts – the latter taking Tarkowski's blast directly in the face.
There are muted handball appeals from the travelling fans, but not from the Everton players.
Everton have lost all eight of their Premier League matches when conceding first this campaign.
Can they fight back here?
Wolves come forward as Cunha drives into the box on the left before seeing a low cross cleared.
It drops to Ait-Nouri, who hammers a volley goalwards but sees it crash off a grey shirt.
It's been an end-to-end start to the second half.

GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! CUNHA MAKES IT TWO! It's a flowing move from the hosts as Sarabia drives infield from the right before slipping a pass between Branthwaite and Keane, finding Hwang running in behind.
He cuts the ball across the face of goal, leaving Cunha with the simplest of finishes at the far post! 2-0 to Wolves!
Wolves' leading goalscorer helps himself to an assist, Hwang putting it on a plate for strike partner Cunha!
It had been a bright start to the second half for Everton, but Wolves look energised by that second goal, knocking the ball around neatly in midfield.

Wolves almost break through on goal again as Joao Gomes finds the run of Ait-Nouri with a terrific line-breaking pass, but the Algeria international sees his pass out towards Cunha cut out by a sliding Branthwaite.
Good defending!
Cunha now has six Premier League goals for the season, with Hwang also on 10.
Wolves didn't have a player score more than the Brazilian across the entirety of 2022-23, with Daniel Podence and Ruben Neves netting six apiece.
POST! A mix-up between Tarkowski and Keane gifts Hwang possession, and the South Korean sits his marker down before giving Pickford the eyes and looking for the near post with his powerful strike.
The goalkeeper gets a slight touch, and it crashes behind off the upright! So close to 3-0!

GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLL! DAWSON WITH THE THIRD! Now Wolves have another! Everton deal with the hosts' corner from the left, but Ait-Nouri stops Calvert-Lewin's break with a fine challenge before offloading to Cunha.
The Brazilian swings in a cross, and Dawson gets across his man to prod into the bottom-left corner, wrongfooting Pickford! Everton truly have a mountain to climb now at 3-0 down!
Cunha has been truly electric in this game, and the former Atletico Madrid man now has a goal and an assist to his name! He also played a prominent role in the opener!
There was a brief VAR check for offside against Dawson, but it was swiftly cleared, much to the delight of the Molineux crowd!
Dyche responds to Wolves' third goal by making two changes.
Coleman is on for Patterson in the first of those.
Andre Gomes replaces Keane as Everton change system.
Everton look to have settled back into their usual 4-5-1 shape now, with Andre Gomes joining Onana and Garner in the engine room.
They struggled to adapt to using a back three, with Tarkowski in particular being dragged all over the place from the right side of defence.
Tarkowski goes into the book for an awful challenge on Cunha, clattering the Brazilian from behind on halfway.
He got a touch to the ball, but you can't tackle like that in the modern game.

OFF THE POST! McNeil almost gets one back for the visitors! The former Burnley man takes aim from 25 yards out, crashing his left-footed effort off the upright and away! That was a warning for Wolves – Sa wasn't getting there.
Great move! Wolves are enjoying themselves now.
Joao Gomes plays a delicate flick into Sarabia, who plays a clever give-and-go with Hwang before feeing it back into the path of Joao Gomes.
The midfielder sits Branthwaite down before hammering a shot at goal, but unfortunately for Wolves, it's straight at Pickford!
GREAT STOP! Pickford denies Wolves a fourth! Cunha plays a great throughball into the path of Hwang, who shoots first-time across goal, looking for the bottom-left corner.
Pickford makes a brilliant reflex save, throwing out a fingertip to tip it wide! Everton are so open at the back!
BALL IN THE NET, BUT THE FLAG IS UP! Cunha teases another great ball in behind Everton's inexplicably high line, allowing Hwang to race through one-on-one.
He makes no mistake, opening his body before bending a shot into the bottom-left corner, but the assistant raises his flag and replays show he was narrowly ahead of the last man.
Unlucky!
O'Neil turns to his bench for the first time.
Ait-Nouri was booked earlier on, and he will be replaced at left wing-back by Hugo Bueno.
Dyche is making another double change.
Beto replaces Calvert-Lewin, who has struggled in attack.
Perhaps more surprisingly, the lively McNeil trudges off.
Danjuma takes his place out wide.
Sarabia pops up on the edge of the box as Wolves look for a fourth, and the Spaniard's shot deflects wide off Tarkowski for a right-wing corner.
Sarabia delivers well from the set-piece, but no gold shirt is attacking it as Onana heads away.
Wolves have now scored 30 goals in the Premier League this season.
They only managed 31 throughout the entirety of last campaign! Their attacking improvement under O'Neil has been huge.
Hwang turns his marker with ease on halfway to set Wolves off on another menacing attack.
The South Korean spreads it wide for Hugo Bueno, who has Cunha and Sarabia to aim for in the centre, but Branthwaite is there to snuff out the danger.
Everton have really struggled with the pace and power of Wolves' front three.

A big cheer goes up around Molineux as the home fans notice Neto stripped and ready to enter the action after two months out! Only Kieran Trippier and Mohamed Salah have matched his seven Premier League assists this season.
Neto replaces Cunha, who gets a standing ovation after an excellent performance.
Sarabia also gets a breather, with Bellegarde on for the final 10 minutes.
Wolves are winless in their final league game in each of the last four calendar years (one draw, three defeats).
That run looks set to end here, unless Everton can produce a remarkable comeback in the next few minutes.
Joao Gomes goes down in midfield as Doyle puts the ball out of play for his team-mate to receive treatment from the medical staff.
Doherty is also on, replacing Semedo in a straight swap at right wing-back.
Joao Gomes is back on his feet and moving freely, but O'Neil opts to withdraw the Brazilian anyway.
Traore takes his place for the final five minutes plus stoppage time.
Everton had won just two of their last 10 away league games against Wolves before this one (four draws, four defeats), winning 3-0 in April 2011 and 2-1 in January 2021.
The Toffees have endured another miserable trip to the West Midlands here.
Everton are still yet to manage a shot on target in this game as we enter the final two minutes of the 90.
Dyche's men simply haven't done enough in the final third, while their most lively forward player – McNeil – was withdrawn after Wolves went 3-0 up.
OVER! Traore skips past Garner in midfield before releasing Neto into the left-hand channel.

Sensing a dream return from injury, the Portugal international drives into the box before letting fly, but his shot spirals over the crossbar and into the South Bank behind the goal! He should have done better.
We will have a minimum of NINE added minutes here.
Nobody is entirely sure where that figure has come from!
Wide! Everton are still yet to record a shot on target as Harrison drives into the area before shooting low, but his effort fades away from Sa's goal to ironic cheers from the home fans.
It really hasn't been the Toffees' day.

THE BALL IS IN THE NET AGAIN, BUT IT WON'T COUNT! Wolves are denied a fourth goal by the linesman once again, much to the relief of Coleman and Pickford! Coleman dwells on the ball under pressure from Hugo Bueno before playing an awkward back pass to Pickford, who sees his return ball picked off by Wolves.
Hwang squares for Neto to side-foot home before wheeling away in celebration, but the flag spoils the hosts' fun – Hwang was offside in the build-up!
Bellegarde screams in pain as he goes down under Branthwaite's challenge.
The Everton defender seemed to accidentally step on his opponent's foot.
There's nothing doing, and the Frenchman is soon back to his feet.
Everton play themselves into trouble once again as Coleman gifts possession to Bellegarde inside the his own box.
His dinked cross is headed up in the air by Branthwaite, then Coleman chests Doherty's second delivery behind for a late corner.
Wolves fail to make anything of the corner, but they won't care.
The final whistle makes it three successive wins for O'Neil's team!
FULL-TIME: WOLVES 3-0 EVERTON.

The full-time whistle sounds at Molineux as Wolves cruise to a third win in six days, crushing Everton 3-0! The hosts started brightly and took the lead after 25 minutes as Kilman prodded home following a scramble inside Everton's six-yard box, and in truth, the Toffees never looked likely to mount a comeback, failing to record a single shot on target.

Cunha made it 2-0 eight minutes into the second half, slamming Hwang's cutback into the roof of the net from close range, then the Brazilian turned provider for the third as Dawson turned his left-wing cross home.

Hwang and Neto both had goals disallowed for offside in the closing stages, but O'Neil won't mind with his team now up to 28 points from 20 games following a very productive festive period! They stay 11th in the Premier League table, level with Chelsea in 10th, while Everton remain just one point above the relegation zone.
That's all from Molineux, so thank you for joining us and Happy New Year!
